title: Artifact provenance + performance fingerprint admission for embedding/reranker models
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Admitting embedding and reranker model artifacts into the pinned-catalog and publishing their performance profiles is currently permissive: manifests and published profiles can diverge from the actual runtime characteristics of the artifact (different quantization, kernels, or packaging). This leads to hard-to-diagnose regressions in latency/cost and occasional incorrect rollback decisions.

Goal: Implement an admission gate that combines (1) artifact provenance metadata (build/container digest, quantization profile, pinned kernel set) and (2) a compact performance fingerprint (latency percentiles, memory footprint, batch-scaling points, and eval accuracy on the onboarding testset). The gate should verify that the provenance is consistent with the declared manifest and that the fingerprint is within an acceptable delta from the pinned profile or is explicitly allowed by an override policy.

Scope: embedding and reranker models only. Deliverables include: fingerprint recorder in the onboarding harness, manifest schema extension for provenance fields, fingerprint DB & comparison API, profile-publisher changes to include fingerprint checks, UI/CLI feedback for admit/deny reasons, CI/integration tests, and rollout plan with canary enforcement and opt-out for early customers.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding harness produces a stable performance fingerprint artifact for embedding and reranker models (JSON blob + hash).
Model manifest schema extended to include provenance fields (build_hash, container_digest, quant_profile, kernel_signature).
Profile publisher refuses to publish a profile if fingerprint mismatch > configured threshold unless explicit override is supplied and audited.
Catalog UI shows fingerprint diff and root-cause hints when a publish is blocked.
Integration tests that simulate: identical artifact, quantization-changed artifact, and kernel-changed artifact with expected admit/deny outcomes pass in CI.
Canary rollout runs for two internal teams and shows no false positives at default thresholds before wider enforcement.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Enable fingerprinting only; store fingerprints in a non-enforced bucket and surface diffs in the console (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (canary): Enforce admission for internal infra + two product teams; send automated audit emails for blocked publishes (3 weeks).
Phase 2 (opt-in customers): Offer opt-in enforcement toggle in Console with clear migration guidance (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (default enforcement): Make gate default for all new publishes; provide escape hatch via customer support and recorded audit trail (2 weeks).
steps: Add fingerprint recorder to onboarding harness: run microbenchmarks that produce percentiles (p50/p90/p99), measured memory working set, and batch scaling curve points under representative input shapes.
Define compact fingerprint JSON schema and canonical hashing algorithm (deterministic ordering + SHA256).
Extend model manifest spec: add provenance.{build_hash,container_digest,quant_profile,kernel_signature} and fingerprint.hash fields.
Implement fingerprint DB and comparison API (HTTP endpoint) that computes normalized distance and returns pass/fail plus salient diffs.
Update profile publisher service: query comparison API during publish; block publish on fail unless override flag and audit metadata present.
Instrument Console: show fingerprint summary, diffs, and suggested remediation (re-run onboarding, update manifest, request trust exception).
Add CI integration tests that stub kernel/quant differences and assert correct gating behavior and audit log entries.
Create migration job to compute fingerprints for current pinned artifacts and seed DB with historical fingerprints for comparison baselines.
Coordinate with Security to ensure provenance fields do not leak sensitive build metadata; encrypt container_digest at rest if required.
Run canary and collect metrics: blocked_publishes, false_positive_rate, time-to-resolve, customer tickets created.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Asha: Kickoff done with PM/Research. Agreed to target embeddings and rerankers first because they have stable eval suites and predictable batching patterns.
2026-03-05 — Liam: Prototype fingerprint recorder implemented (p50/p90/p99 + mem + batch scaling) and validated on three internal models. Recorded hashes are stable across deterministic runs.
2026-03-07 — Marisol (PM): Requested that mismatch reasons be surfaced in plain language (e.g., 'quantization changed: 8-bit vs 4-bit'). Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-09 — Security review note: avoid publishing full build metadata to public console. We will store container_digest and build_hash in the catalog DB but only show truncated hash in UI; full values require audit permissions.

2026-03-11 — Code review feedback (ENG): ask to normalize latency measurements to a fixed token-length distribution and include a 'warmup' phase to stabilize KV cache behavior. Liam updated harness accordingly.
2026-03-14 — Liam: Implemented comparison API and schema changes; integration tests added. Next: seed migration job and Console UI prototyping.
